_about: hermes-viz's own settings definitions. This is the whole surface: no `config_schema` lives in plugin.yaml, so the app folds no auto-generated form under the plugin's Settings page and the plugin owns its fields, defaults and validation. dashboard/plugin_api.py reads this file for both its field list and its _coerce(). Values still live at plugins.entries.hermes-viz.settings.<key> and the agent half still reads them through ctx.get_config.

palette.label: Diagram palette
palette.description: Which palette is baked into derived diagrams. Mermaid draws into an isolated , so its colours cannot follow the app's theme live.

max_widgets.label: Widgets per answer
max_widgets.description: Upper bound on the widgets derived from one answer, so a long numeric answer does not turn into a wall of charts.

rule_groups.label: Active rule groups
rule_groups.description: Which rule groups from rules.yaml may fire. A group that is off leaves the prompt and the derivation; an explicit `::viz` still draws.

body_style.label: Style the answer body
body_style.description: One centred column for the whole turn — the prose, the drawings and the run of tool work between them — and the accent on headings. It reaches into the host DOM, so CI cannot check the pixels.

font_body.label: Body face
font_body.description: The face the answer's prose and a widget's values are set in. System declares nothing, leaving the app's own face; a shipped family travels inside the plugin as data. Desktop only, and the pixels are not verifiable from here.

font_heading.label: Heading face
font_heading.description: The face a widget's title and section head are set in. System declares nothing, leaving the app's own face; a shipped family travels inside the plugin as data. Desktop only, and the pixels are not verifiable from here.

chrome_composer.label: Composer
chrome_composer.description: Room for a paragraph in the input before it scrolls, a roomier surface and one hairline of lift — and the conversation reads through it: the input's fill is thinner, with a blur over the words behind it that grows toward the top, so what is scrolling away dissolves instead of being capped by a box. Moves the app's own height, padding and fill tokens; nothing the app already draws is restated. Desktop only, and the pixels are not verifiable from here.

chrome_surfaces.label: Menus and dialogs
chrome_surfaces.description: Menus, popovers and dialogs a shade rounder and glassier than the app draws them — a thinner fill over a stronger blur, so what sits behind a menu stays legible through it. Desktop only, and the pixels are not verifiable from here.

chrome_panes.label: Pane cards
chrome_panes.description: Every pane drawn as one rounded card: 6px of room on the sides that meet the window's own border, none on the side that meets the conversation, and 3px at a seam between two panes. The card is a faint wash of the theme's ink, never an opaque fill, so the window stays as translucent as you set it. The conversation column gets no frame and no surface at all, and the terminal's frame follows the pane too — the shell's own text area is the one block a stylesheet cannot make see-through. Desktop only, and the pixels are not verifiable from here.

column_width.label: Session width
column_width.description: A px cap on the reading column — the answer, its drawings and the composer move together and stay aligned with each other. 0 keeps the sheet's own 68ch measure. Desktop only, and the pixels are not verifiable from here.

format_guide.label: Answer format guide
format_guide.description: Adds the answer-structuring prompt to every request: sections, lists, tables, and which kind to draw for what. The live cost is in the chip above.
